drafted_from: tool:make-a-frame-contact-sheet-of-a-video-section row in tool-rows.json, do-work/make_contact_sheet.py and test/make-contact-sheet.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me what happens from second 10 to second 50 of https://video.example/watch/abc as one picture, a frame every 4 seconds, and put it in the folder work/sheets." It runs the command on your computer and opens the sheet it makes.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it makes a clip, a sheet and a log in the folder you give it and keeps no rows.
instructions: 1. Install what it needs once: clone the Workshop repository and brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp (yt-dlp only for a link).
2. Say which video (a link yt-dlp can read, or a file on your computer) and which part, start and end in seconds at most 300 apart; give a short name for the files and a folder.

3. Your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs `python3 trillion-workshop/tools/make-a-frame-contact-sheet-of-a-video-section/do-work/make_contact_sheet.py --source '<link or file>' --name <name> --start <s> --end <e> --folder <folder>`, adding --step N and --cols N to change the spacing and row width.

4. Read the last line: {"result": {"sheet", "clip", "log", "columns", "rows"}} names the picture to open and look at before describing the section; {"result": {"error", "log", "log_tail"}} with exit 1 shows which program failed and the log's last lines.

worked_examples.title: Forty seconds of a linked video, a frame every four seconds
worked_examples.ask: Show me what happens from 10 to 50 seconds of https://video.example/watch/abc as one picture.
worked_examples.given: From tools/make-a-frame-contact-sheet-of-a-video-section/test/make-contact-sheet.test.mjs (yt-dlp and ffmpeg stood in for): the command line is `python3 trillion-workshop/tools/make-a-frame-contact-sheet-of-a-video-section/do-work/make_contact_sheet.py --source 'https://video.example/watch/abc' --name abc --start 10 --end 50 --folder work/sheets`. yt-dlp fetches only *10-50 at 360p or less into work/sheets/clips/abc-10-50.webm, then ffmpeg tiles fps=1/4, 320 pixels wide, 4 columns by 3 rows.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result": {"sheet": "work/sheets/frames/abc-10-50-sheet.jpg", "clip": "work/sheets/clips/abc-10-50.webm", "log": "work/sheets/frames/abc-10-50.log", "columns": 4, "rows": 3}} and the exit status is 0. Run again, the clip already in clips/ is used and yt-dlp is not called. With --end 301 it answers {"result": {"error": "start and end must satisfy 0 <= start < end and cover at most 300 s"}} with exit 2.
